headline: Alberta referendum defeated
dek: 76-77% federalist / 23% separatist with >1M counted: Strongly supported. Vote was nonbinding, on starting a separation process (not independence itself).
sources: Elections Alberta tallies; CBC/CTV projections; official statements (Carney, Premier Danielle Smith); AFP on-the-ground
fault_line: Did 76% kill the separatist dream — or is this just round one with Trump's 51st-state threats in the background?

sections.what_happened: 76-77% federalist / 23% separatist with >1M counted: Strongly supported. Vote was nonbinding, on starting a separation process (not independence itself). Carney frames as unity win amid Trump's trade war and annexation threats. Separatist leader Jeffrey Rath: push continues. Alberta Prosperity Project leaders earlier met US State Department officials (attributed relay via hromadske.ua).
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera, CNA, Saudi Gazette, Gulf News, JPost, hromadske.ua, lokmattimes.
sections.what_disputed: Separatists dismiss the defeat ('this movement is not going to stop'). Poll delays at 100+ stations extended voting hours.
sections.why_matters: Carney's unity win is really a verdict on Trump's annexation threats — but the separatists' US State Department meetings say this fight isn't over.
sections.context: Background: Alberta referendum defeated: ~76% back remaining in Canada; separatists vow to continue

totw_analysis: Our read: Carney's unity win is really a verdict on Trump's annexation threats — but the separatists' US State Department meetings say this fight isn't over. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did 76% kill the separatist dream — or is this just round one with Trump's 51st-state threats in the background?
